note: Clinical concepts proposed from the literature. Every concept starts as a candidate. A candidate is never shown to a live answer and never enforced. It becomes enforced only when (1) its test cases pass at its current content (knowledge.py test) and (2) the clinical reviewer approves that exact content (knowledge.py review). Any edit to a concept's content after review returns it to candidate. Codes and thresholds are stated so they can be checked; the summary is in our own words.

concepts.name: CKD GFR categories (G1 to G5)
concepts.summary: KDIGO GFR categories in mL/min/1.73 m2: G1 90 or more, G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 under 15. CKD stage 3 is eGFR 30-59 (G3a plus G3b). A CKD diagnosis needs the abnormality to last more than 3 months (for example two eGFR results under 60 at least 90 days apart); a single low eGFR is reduced kidney function, not CKD. Unless the question says otherwise, use each patient's eGFR results in the period; say whether a single result or two results 90 days apart were required.

retrieves: How many patients have stage 3 CKD by eGFR?
Patients with an eGFR under 30 in 2028
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'egfr' AND value_canonical >= 30 AND value_canonical < 60
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'egfr' AND value_canonical < 45
tests.check_question: How many patients had stage 3 CKD by eGFR in 2028?

concepts.name: Albuminuria categories (A1 to A3)
concepts.summary: KDIGO albuminuria categories by urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR) in mg/g: A1 under 30 (normal to mildly increased), A2 30-300 (moderately increased, once called microalbuminuria), A3 over 300 (severely increased). Albuminuria means uACR 30 mg/g or more. A uACR is a ratio; a urine albumin concentration alone (mg/L) is not a uACR.

retrieves: How many patients with diabetes have albuminuria?
patients with a UACR over 300
ignores: How many flu shots were given in 2028?
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'uacr' AND value_canonical >= 30
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'uacr' AND value_canonical > 20

concepts.name: Acute kidney injury (KDIGO creatinine criteria)
concepts.triggers: acute kidney injury|\baki\b|acute renal failure|creatinine (?:rise|increase|jump)|kidney injur
concepts.summary: KDIGO AKI by serum creatinine: a rise of 0.3 mg/dL or more within 48 hours, or a rise to 1.5 times baseline or more within 7 days (baseline = the lowest creatinine in the prior 7 days when no earlier baseline is known); urine output under 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 hours also qualifies but is rarely in claims or lab tables. Stages by creatinine: 1 = 1.5-1.9 times baseline or +0.3; 2 = 2.0-2.9 times; 3 = 3 times or more, or 4.0 mg/dL or more, or dialysis started. With dates only (no times), 48 hours is approximated by results up to 2 days apart; say so. A coded diagnosis of AKI is ICD-10-CM N17.

retrieves: How many patients had acute kidney injury by creatinine in 2028?
AKI events by lab criteria
ignores: How many patients had a creatinine test in 2028?
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM measurement a JOIN measurement b ON a.patient_id = b.patient_id WHERE a.concept = 'creatinine' AND b.concept = 'creatinine' AND b.value_canonical - a.value_canonical >= 0.3
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'creatinine' AND value_canonical > 1.2
tests.check_question: How many patients had acute kidney injury by creatinine in 2028?

concepts.name: Diabetes and prediabetes by HbA1c and glucose (ADA)
concepts.triggers: undiagnosed diabetes|prediabet|pre-diabet|diabetic range|meets? (?:the )?(?:criteria|definition) for diabetes|diabetes (?:by|on) (?:lab|a1c|hba1c|glucose)|could have diabetes|likely diabet
concepts.summary: ADA diagnostic thresholds: diabetes is HbA1c 6.5% or more, fasting plasma glucose 126 mg/dL or more, 2-hour glucose 200 mg/dL or more on an oral glucose tolerance test, or a random glucose 200 mg/dL or more with symptoms; without symptoms, two abnormal results are needed. Prediabetes is HbA1c 5.7-6.4% or fasting glucose 100-125 mg/dL. A random (non-fasting) glucose below 200 does not diagnose anything; lab tables usually do not say whether a glucose was fasting. 'Undiagnosed diabetes' means a diabetic-range result in a patient with no diabetes diagnosis on record (ICD-10-CM E08-E13).

retrieves: How many patients have an HbA1c in the diabetic range but no diabetes diagnosis?
How many patients have prediabetes by A1c?

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'hba1c' AND value_canonical >= 7
tests.check_question: How many patients have undiagnosed diabetes?

concepts.name: Hypoglycemia levels (ADA)
concepts.summary: ADA hypoglycemia levels: level 1 is glucose under 70 mg/dL and at or above 54; level 2 (clinically significant) is under 54 mg/dL; level 3 is a severe event needing another person's help, with no glucose threshold. 'Hypoglycemia' by lab means glucose under 70 mg/dL unless a level is named. Coded hypoglycemia: ICD-10-CM E16.0-E16.2, E10.649, E11.649.

concepts.name: CMS122 glycemic status above 9% (poor control)
concepts.triggers: poor(?:ly)? (?:glycemic )?control|uncontrolled diabet|a1c (?:over|above|greater than|>) ?9|hba1c (?:over|above|greater than|>) ?9|cms ?122|glycemic status|diabetes control
concepts.summary: CMS122 (an inverse measure; lower is better): patients 18-75 with diabetes and a qualifying visit in the year. Numerator: the most recent glycemic status result in the year (HbA1c, or glucose management indicator) is above 9.0%, OR there is no result in the year. A patient with no HbA1c in the year counts as poorly controlled. Exclusions include hospice, palliative care, and 66 or older with frailty and advanced illness. 'Above 9' is strictly greater than 9.0.

concepts.name: CMS165 controlling high blood pressure
concepts.triggers: controll?(?:ed|ing) (?:high )?(?:blood pressure|bp|hypertension)|blood pressure control|bp control|cms ?165|hypertension (?:is |are )?(?:controlled|under control)|uncontrolled (?:hypertension|blood pressure|bp)
concepts.summary: CMS165: patients 18-85 with essential hypertension diagnosed before or during the first six months of the year, with a visit in the year. Numerator: the most recent blood pressure in the year is adequately controlled, systolic under 140 AND diastolic under 90. When several readings share the most recent date, use the lowest systolic and the lowest diastolic of that day. No reading in the year counts as not controlled. Exclusions include hospice, palliative care, end-stage renal disease, dialysis, kidney transplant, pregnancy, and 66 or older with frailty and advanced illness.

concepts.name: CMS347 statin therapy benefit groups
concepts.triggers: statin benefit|should be on a statin|eligible for (?:a )?statin|statin therapy for (?:the )?prevention|cms ?347|statin gap|missing (?:a )?statin
concepts.summary: CMS347 counts patients in any of three statin benefit groups who were prescribed or were on statin therapy in the year: (1) clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (coronary disease, myocardial infarction, stroke or TIA, peripheral arterial disease, revascularization), any adult age; (2) age 20 or older with any LDL of 190 mg/dL or more, or familial hypercholesterolemia; (3) age 40-75 with diabetes. Exclusions include statin allergy or adverse effect, rhabdomyolysis, pregnancy or breastfeeding, end-stage renal disease, cirrhosis, hospice and palliative care.

concepts.name: HFrEF and guideline-directed medical therapy (four classes)
concepts.triggers: \bgdmt\b|guideline[- ]directed|hfref|reduced ejection fraction|reduced ef|four pillars|quadruple therapy|optimal medical therapy for heart failure
concepts.summary: HFrEF is heart failure with LVEF 40% or less (2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA). Guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF is four classes: (1) a renin-angiotensin inhibitor - ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) preferred, else ACE inhibitor or ARB; (2) an evidence-based beta blocker - carvedilol, metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol only (other beta blockers do not count); (3) a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (spironolactone, eplerenone); (4) an SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin). 'On GDMT' or 'quadruple therapy' means all four classes; say if a looser count (any one, or three of four) is used. Coded HFrEF is ICD-10-CM I50.2x (systolic) or I50.4x (combined).

sources.where: Section 7.3, stage C HFrEF pharmacological treatment

retrieves: How many HFrEF patients are on all four GDMT classes?
patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction on guideline-directed therapy
ignores: How many heart failure admissions in 2028?

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM fill WHERE drug_class = 'beta_blocker'
tests.check_question: How many HFrEF patients are on GDMT?

concepts.name: Natriuretic peptide thresholds for heart failure (ESC)
concepts.summary: 2021 ESC: heart failure is unlikely in a non-acute setting with NT-proBNP under 125 pg/mL (BNP under 35); in an acute setting the rule-out is NT-proBNP under 300 pg/mL (BNP under 100). 'Elevated NT-proBNP' therefore means 125 pg/mL or more out of hospital, 300 or more in acute care; say which.

sources.where: Section 4.1, diagnostic algorithm; Section 11, acute HF

concepts.name: Iron deficiency (general and in heart failure)
concepts.summary: In heart failure (2021 ESC) iron deficiency is ferritin under 100 ng/mL, or ferritin 100-299 ng/mL with transferrin saturation (TSAT) under 20%. Outside heart failure, ferritin under 30 ng/mL is a common adult cutoff for iron deficiency (WHO uses under 15 in healthy adults); inflammation raises ferritin. Sources differ outside heart failure: state the cutoff used. TSAT is LOINC 2502-3 (iron / total iron-binding capacity).

retrieves: How many heart failure patients are iron deficient?

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'ferritin' AND value_canonical < 30
tests.check_question: How many heart failure patients are iron deficient?

concepts.name: Anaemia by haemoglobin (WHO adult cutoffs)
concepts.summary: WHO 2024 adult cutoffs: anaemia is haemoglobin under 13.0 g/dL in men and under 12.0 g/dL in non-pregnant women (ages 15-65; the same cutoffs are used for older adults). The cutoff depends on sex: a single cutoff for everyone is wrong. Severity (non-pregnant adults): mild 11.0 to just under the cutoff, moderate 8.0-10.9, severe under 8.0 g/dL. A coded anaemia diagnosis is ICD-10-CM D50-D64.

retrieves: How many patients were anemic by hemoglobin in 2028?
ignores: How many patients had a platelet count?

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'hemoglobin' AND value_canonical < 12

concepts.name: Hyperkalaemia thresholds (sources differ)
concepts.summary: Sources differ on the threshold. Many laboratories and the KDIGO controversies conference treat potassium above 5.0 mmol/L as hyperkalaemia; the European Resuscitation Council uses 5.5 mmol/L or more, with 6.5 or more severe (6.0-6.4 moderate). When a question says 'hyperkalemia' without a number and no customer definition settles it, the two cutoffs are two readings: ask which, or give both.

concepts.summary: European clinical practice guideline (2014): hyponatraemia is serum sodium under 135 mmol/L; mild 130-134, moderate 125-129, profound under 125 mmol/L. Coded hyponatraemia is ICD-10-CM E87.1.

concepts.name: Sepsis: Sepsis-3, SIRS and coded sepsis
concepts.summary: Sepsis-3 (2016): life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated response to infection, operationalised as suspected infection plus a rise in SOFA score of 2 or more; septic shock is sepsis needing vasopressors to keep mean arterial pressure 65 mmHg or more with lactate above 2 mmol/L despite fluids. SIRS (1992, used by SEP-1): two or more of temperature over 38 or under 36 C, heart rate over 90, respiratory rate over 20 (or PaCO2 under 32 mmHg), white count over 12 or under 4 x10^3/uL (or over 10% bands). SOFA needs PaO2/FiO2, platelets, bilirubin, vasopressors, Glasgow score and creatinine or urine output; most warehouses cannot compute it, so a Sepsis-3 count from data usually rests on coded sepsis: ICD-10-CM A40, A41, R65.20 (severe sepsis) and R65.21 (septic shock), and A02.1, A22.7, A26.7, A32.7, A39.4, B37.7 for organism-specific sepsis.

not_computable.needs: SOFA components (PaO2/FiO2, bilirubin, vasopressor doses, Glasgow Coma Scale, urine output) with times; the warehouse has none of the respiratory, neurological or vasopressor parts

retrieves: How many septic shock admissions in 2028?

concepts.name: Lactate thresholds in sepsis (SEP-1, Sepsis-3)
concepts.summary: Lactate is reported in mmol/L. SEP-1: an initial lactate above 2 mmol/L requires a repeat lactate within 6 hours of severe sepsis presentation; a lactate of 4 mmol/L or more requires 30 mL/kg of crystalloid within 3 hours. Sepsis-3 septic shock uses lactate above 2 mmol/L. 'Elevated lactate' means above 2 mmol/L unless 4 or more is named. In lab tables lactate is LOINC 2524-7 (serum or plasma) or 32693-4 (blood).

concepts.name: SEP-1 bundle compliance needs times
concepts.triggers: sep-?1|sepsis bundle|bundle complian|time to antibiotic|antibiotics? within (?:1|one|3|three) hours?
concepts.summary: SEP-1 compliance needs the time of severe sepsis presentation and the times of each bundle element (lactate drawn, blood cultures before antibiotics, broad-spectrum antibiotics within 3 hours, repeat lactate within 6 hours, fluids and vasopressors for shock, repeat volume status assessment). It is abstracted from charts. Without order and administration times it cannot be computed.

concepts.name: NHSN device-associated infections (CAUTI, CLABSI) need device days and cultures
concepts.summary: NHSN CAUTI and CLABSI are surveillance definitions: an infection window with a positive culture meeting organism and colony-count criteria, a device in place more than 2 consecutive days, symptoms, and a hospital-onset date (day 3 or later). Rates are per 1,000 device days; the standardized infection ratio (SIR) divides observed by NHSN-predicted infections. Diagnosis codes are not a substitute. Without device days, culture results and NHSN predicted counts it cannot be computed.

not_computable.needs: device days (urinary catheter or central line), culture results with organisms and dates, and NHSN predicted counts; the warehouse has none of them

concepts.name: Potentially inappropriate medications in older adults (AGS Beers 2023, selected classes)
concepts.summary: The AGS Beers Criteria (2023) list medications older adults (65 and older) should generally avoid. Classes the warehouse can see by drug class include: benzodiazepines; first-generation antihistamines; skeletal muscle relaxants; sulfonylureas (avoid as first- or second-line therapy); chronic NSAIDs unless alternatives fail; proton pump inhibitors beyond 8 weeks unless high risk; antipsychotics except for schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. Beers is criteria, not a single measure: name which classes are counted. Age is 65 or older at the fill date.

concepts.name: Concurrent opioid and benzodiazepine use
concepts.summary: FDA (2016 boxed warning) and CDC (2022 guideline) warn against combining opioids and benzodiazepines (respiratory depression and death). Concurrent use means the days' supply of an opioid fill and a benzodiazepine fill overlap (each fill covers fill date through fill date plus days supplied minus 1). The PQA COB measure is stricter: adults 18 and older with 2 or more fills of each on different dates and 30 or more cumulative days of overlap, excluding cancer, sickle cell disease, hospice and palliative care. Overlap of any day and the 30-day measure are two readings; say which.

readings.label: any day of overlapping supply
readings.rule: supplies overlap by at least one day

readings.label: PQA COB: 30 or more days of overlap, 2 or more fills each

check_passes: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.patient_id) FROM fill a JOIN fill b ON a.patient_id = b.patient_id WHERE a.drug_class = 'opioid' AND b.drug_class = 'benzodiazepine' AND a.fill_date <= b.supply_end AND b.fill_date <= a.supply_end

concepts.name: 'Triple whammy': NSAID with a RAS blocker and a diuretic
concepts.summary: The 'triple whammy' is concurrent use of an NSAID, an ACE inhibitor or ARB, and a diuretic (loop or thiazide). In a nested case-control study (Lapi 2013) it raised the rate of acute kidney injury by about 31%, most in the first 30 days. Concurrent means the three days' supplies overlap on at least one day (fill date through fill date plus days supplied minus 1). Potassium-sparing MRAs are not counted as the diuretic unless the question says so.

concepts.name: Obesity by BMI (CDC adult categories)

concepts.name: Atrial fibrillation and oral anticoagulation
concepts.summary: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS: oral anticoagulation (warfarin or a direct oral anticoagulant: apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, dabigatran) is recommended for atrial fibrillation with an annual stroke risk of 2% or more, commonly CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or more in men and 3 or more in women. Aspirin or other antiplatelet drugs are not an alternative to anticoagulation for stroke prevention and do not count as anticoagulation. Coded atrial fibrillation is ICD-10-CM I48.

concepts.name: AHRQ PQI 08 heart failure admission rate
concepts.summary: AHRQ Prevention Quality Indicators count admissions for ambulatory care sensitive conditions per 100,000 adult residents (18 and older) per year. PQI 08 (heart failure): admissions of adults with a principal diagnosis of heart failure (I50 codes, and hypertensive heart or heart-and-kidney disease with heart failure, I11.0, I13.0, I13.2), excluding transfers in from another facility and admissions with cardiac procedures. PQI 01 (diabetes short-term complications): principal diagnosis of diabetes with ketoacidosis, hyperosmolarity or coma. The denominator is the adult population, not the admitted patients; the rate is per 100,000.

retrieves: What is our PQI 08 heart failure admission rate for 2028?

concepts.name: Polypharmacy (definitions vary)
concepts.summary: A systematic review (Masnoon 2017) found the most common definition of polypharmacy is five or more medications used at the same time; ten or more is often called hyperpolypharmacy. Definitions differ on whether medications are counted at one point in time or over a period, and on whether classes or individual drugs are counted. Count concurrent supplies (overlapping days' supply) of distinct drugs or classes, and say which.

retrieves: How many older patients have polypharmacy?
